messages:
sara_support: FYI customer org_42 reported a big invoice spike on 2026-03-12 — billed tokens ~1.2M but their dashboard shows ~800k served. Sample req_id: req_0a1b2c. Can we triage? :thinking:

 tom_billing: Thanks, Sara. Can you paste the invoice line items and any meter IDs? Wondering if warmup/prefetch tokens were included in the invoice. Also any trace ids or example request ids will help.

 billing-bot: Invoice 2026-03-12 | org_42 | billed_tokens=1204123 | meter=tokenizer.v1 | line_item=warmup_prefetch | invoice_id=inv_7654

 alex_runtime: Possible angle: continuous batching + prefix/KV prefetch interaction. We've seen cases where prefetch increments the metered counter, then the actual request lands in an overlapping batch and also gets metered — resulting in billed > served. Need logs to confirm (look for prefetch=true, batch_id).

 nina_sre: @sara can you try a quick repro? Send a burst of requests with the same prefix and include debug metrics in the request header (X-Debug-Metrics). Check runtime logs for `metered_tokens` vs `served_tokens`.

 sara_support: Repro steps I used below — quick loop that mimics the customer workload (sent as background jobs):

 ```bash
 for i in {1..50}; do
   curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n     -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \n     -H \"X-Debug-Metrics: true\" \n     -d '{"model":"gpt-small","prompt":"prefix_'$i' long_prompt_repeated...","stream":false}' &
 done
 wait
 ```

 I captured runtime logs for a few req_ids. here's a trimmed snippet showing the odd double-metering behavior: 

 ```text
 [2026-03-12T10:02:12Z] req=req_0a1b2c batch_id=batch_77 prefetch=true metered_tokens+=512
 [2026-03-12T10:02:12Z] req=req_0a1b2c batch_id=batch_80 prefetch=false served_tokens+=512
 [2026-03-12T10:02:12Z] req=req_0a1b2c metered_counter=1024 served_counter=512
 ```

 alex_runtime: That log pattern is the tell — same req_id hit a prefetch path (batch_77) and then was included in the continuous batch (batch_80). Prefetch path increments the metering early; continuous batch increments again when actually served. We should be deduping meter increments by req_id or marking prefetch as non-billable if served soon after.

 nina_sre: Agreed. Short-term mitigation: reduce prefetch window for org_42 or turn off prefetch for them. Long-term: enforce an idempotent meter hook keyed by (org_id, req_id) so prefetch doesn't double-charge.

 tom_billing: For remediation I'll prepare a pro-rated credit for the delta (approx 400k tokens) and open billing ticket BT-2319. @sara can you DM me the full list of affected req_ids + timestamps so I can attach them to the ticket?

 sara_support: Sending the list to you now via DM. Also flagged a runtime issue with @alex_runtime and @nina_sre for follow-up on dedupe and prefetch logic. Thanks all :heart:

 alex_runtime: I'll add a short reproducer test in the runtime repo and a monitor that alerts when billed/served ratio > 1.15 for any org.

 nina_sre: I'll schedule a rollback-safe flag to disable prefetch per-org while we patch.

 tom_billing: Filed credit and CC'd finance. Will update customer once we confirm patch window. :white_check_mark:
